## 1. Pepper Mushroom Rice
**@ral.livezy** · 2026-10-10 · video · ❤ 73075 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DeTayF4zMJX/

Pepper Mushroom Rice

Recipe by @pawar_omkar 

Ingredients:
To a pot on medium heat, add 2 tbsp ghee
Add 2 sliced green chillies 
15 curry leaves
1/2 tsp hing
Sliced onions (200g)
Sauté until the onions turn golden brown.

Meanwhile, using a mortar and pestle, crush 2 tsp black peppercorns with 7 garlic cloves into a coarse paste.

Add the paste to the pot
Then add 2 tbsp biryani masala
1 tsp salt
500g mushrooms, cut in half

Mix everything well and let the mushrooms cook for 3 minutes.

Now add 400g washed raw rice and 2 cups of hot water. Give everything a good mix.

Once it comes to a boil, reduce the flame to low, cover with a lid, and let it cook for 15 minutes or until the rice is fully cooked.

Remove the lid, garnish with freshly chopped coriander, and it’s ready to serve!

Nutrition (Entire Dish Serves 4)
Calories per serving - 478 cal
Protein - 11g
Carbs - 90g
Fats - 8g

## 4. Creamiestt Mushroom Pasta 🍄 🍝
**@junkdecoded** · 2026-09-25 · video · ❤ 4238 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DdoFCRsgoAw/

Creamiestt Mushroom Pasta 🍄 🍝

Ingredients

* 200 g whole wheat/ semolina pasta
* 250 g low-fat paneer
* 2 cheese cubes
* 3–4 cashews
* Mushrooms
* 1 onion
* 3–4 garlic cloves
* Salt, pepper & chilli flakes
* Little pasta water as needed

Recipe:
Boil the pasta. Blend paneer, cashews and sufficient water until veryyyy smooth, creamy and runnyy. Sauté garlic, onion + mushrooms, add the creamy sauce and boiled pasta, keep adding water until you get milk like consistency in the white sauce, boil for 1 min, top with cheese cube and seasonings. Always eat hot! 🤌

If divided into 4 servings:
~335 kcal | ~25 g protein per serving 🔥

## 5. HOMEMADE SODA SERIES EP 5 ✨
**@caprililly** · 2026-09-24 · video · ❤ 2246 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DdrZgOUBpXo/

HOMEMADE SODA SERIES EP 5 ✨

This is my naturally carbonated Carrot Orange Ginger Turmeric Soda, inspired by everyone’s favorite “retinol juice,” but turned into a probiotic-rich soda using a turmeric bug.

Carrots bring beta-carotene, which the body can convert into vitamin A. Oranges add vitamin C to support collagen production. Ginger adds that spicy kick, and turmeric brings curcumin, a plant compound known for its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory benefits.

The result is bright, golden, lightly sweet, naturally fizzy, and so refreshing.

🥕Retinol Soda
FOR THE FRESH JUICE (Makes about 2 cups)

▪️4–5 carrots
▪️2 oranges
▪️1 lemon
▪️2-inch piece fresh ginger
▪️1 apple (optional)

When Bottling the drink

▪️2.5cups of fresh pressed carrot ginger juice
▪️1 cup coconut water
▪️⅓ cup active turmeric bug
▪️Pinch of black pepper
▪️Optional: 1–2 tbsp maple syrup or honey, to sweeten the drink when bottling because the turmeric bug eats most of the natural sugars in the drink.

Add everything to a fermentation-safe bottle, leaving a little room at the top. Seal and let ferment at room temperature for 1–3 days, depending on how warm your kitchen is and how active your turmeric bug is. Once fizzy, refrigerate overnight before opening slowly.

🌽 Crispy Corn Bhajia

Golden, crispy and packed with fresh corn, herbs and spices! these homemade corn bhajia are the perfect snack with chai or your favourite chutney🔥

Ingredients

* 4 corn on the cobs, grated
* 1 red onion, finely chopped
* ⅓ cup chickpea flour (besan), plus extra as needed
* 1 tbsp ginger
* 1 tbsp green chilli
* 1 tbsp fresh coriander
* 1 small garlic clove
* 1 tbsp ajwain (carom seeds)
* 1 handful fresh fenugreek leaves (methi)
* 1 tbsp salt
* 1 tbsp fresh lime juice
* 1½ tbsp oil
* Oil, for deep frying

Method

1. Prepare the corn
  Grate the corn off the cobs into a large mixing bowl.
2. Add the chickpea flour
  Add ⅓ cup chickpea flour to the grated corn and mix well.
3. Add the onion & aromatics
  Finely chop the red onion and add it to the mixture. Blitz the ginger, green chilli, coriander and garlic, then add this to the bowl.
4. Season
  Add the ajwain, fresh fenugreek leaves, salt, lime juice and 1½ tbsp oil. Mix everything together thoroughly.
5. Adjust the consistency
  Let the mixture sit for around 10–15 minutes. The corn and onion will release moisture as it rests. If the mixture feels too runny, add a little more chickpea flour …

## 11. Soya burger salad 🥗🍔
**@batati.being.batati** · 2026-09-09 · video · ❤ 40151 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DdESTY5qemK/

Soya burger salad 🥗🍔

🌱Ingredients

* 60 g dry soya chunks
* 150 g plain skyr 
* ½ tsp oil
* ½ tsp red chilli powder
* ¼ tsp turmeric
* ½ tsp burger/pizza seasoning
* Salt
* 1 tsp mustard sauce
* 1 tsp red chilli sauce
* ½ tsp honey
* 1 cup lettuce
* ½ cucumber
* ¼ onion
* Coriander

✅Method

1. Soak 60 g soya chunks in hot salted water for 10–15 minutes.
2. Squeeze them really well. This is important for getting that meaty texture.
3. Heat ½ tsp oil in a kadhai. Add soya, chilli powder, turmeric, seasoning and salt.
4. Sauté on medium-high heat until the soya becomes nicely roasted and slightly crispy.
5. In a bowl, mix 150 g skyr + mustard + chilli sauce + ½ tsp honey.
6. Add lettuce, cucumber and onion.
7. Add the hot masala soya and toss everything together.
8. Finish with coriander.

## 19. 🤯 I’ve been kicking myself over this…. WHY HAVEN’T I BEEN MEAL PREPPING LIKE THIS ALL ALONG?!
**@little.vegan.eats** · 2026-08-22 · video · ❤ 69028 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DcVpt8bxooY/

🤯 I’ve been kicking myself over this…. WHY HAVEN’T I BEEN MEAL PREPPING LIKE THIS ALL ALONG?!

This is what I’m calling Duplo Dinners, and it has completely changed the way I freeze and prep meals. Instead of freezing one full meal, you prep and freeze each component separately: grains, sauces, proteins, and veggies… like building blocks. Mostly these are leftovers from double cooking a recipe, so there’s no actual extra work and you can slowly stock your freezer supply over a month. 

Then, when you need a quick meal, you can mix and match different combos to create endless healthy, nourishing, and varied dinners or lunches (& your kids can pick what they want, or for when they don’t like what’s on offer for dinner). It’s like having your own little satisfying adult Lego set in the freezer 🙌🏼. 

Our containers are from @seedandsproutco which are the perfect portion size: I find 3 blocks (a protein, a grain, and a veg base) works for our 4 year old and 5-6 blocks works for adults. Then you just pop them in your glass container, defrost in the fridge overnight, warm it up however you like, and enjoy! 

In this reel the recipes I made are:
🌶 Vegan Chilli Sin Carne
🥣 Vegan Sour Cream
🍛 Vegan Katsu Sauce (I have this multiple times a week 🤤)
🍠 Roasted Sweet Potato
🥬 Steamed Greens 
🌱 Marinated Tofu Cubes
🥕 Roasted Chickpeas
🍚 Quinoa
🍘 Brown Rice

Let’s get the freezers …

## 23. High Protein, Iron Rich Theplas 
**@vaishali_living** · 2026-08-17 · video · ❤ 2690 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DcISnHHB9uS/

High Protein, Iron Rich Theplas 

1 serving (2–3 theplas) — ~25g protein
💪 High Protein | Soft & Thin | Makes 7–8 theplas

Ingredients

🍀 200g whole wheat flour
🍀 50g besan
🍀 2 cups red amaranth leaves, finely chopped
🍀 ¼ cup dahi
🍀 1 scoop whey isolate (30g protein)
🍀 1 tbsp cumin powder
🍀 1 tsp coriander powder
🍀 ½ tsp turmeric
🍀 ½ tsp ajwain
🍀 ½–1 tsp Kashmiri/red chilli powder
🍀 ½ tsp amchur powder
🍀 1-inch ginger, grated
🍀 3–4 garlic cloves, grated
🍀 1–2 green chillies, finely chopped
🍀 Salt, to taste
🍀 Water, as needed
🍀 Ghee, for cooking

Method

🍀 Add wheat flour, besan, whey, chopped amaranth, dahi and all the spices to a large bowl. Mix well.

🍀 Add very little water at first—the amaranth and dahi will release moisture as the dough rests. Knead into a soft, pliable dough, then rest for 10–15 minutes. Add a little more water only if needed.

🍀 Divide into 7–8 portions and roll each one as thin as possible, just like a soft chapati.

🍀 Heat a tawa and cook the thepla on one side. Flip, apply a little ghee, flip again, then apply ghee on the other side.

🍀 Cook until both sides develop beautiful golden spots and the thepla is completely cooked through.

🍀 Serve hot with dahi, achar, chutney or your favourite sabzi.

## 24. 🥣 High Protein Breakfast Series | Ep 4
**@living.with.niharika** · 2026-08-17 · video · ❤ 53763 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DcIJo7TtpBF/

🥣 High Protein Breakfast Series | Ep 4

Creamy, savory Paneer Oats packed with veggies and protein — an easy breakfast that keeps you full and comes together in one pan!

💪 Macros per serving
Protein: ~20g
Calories: ~350 kcal

Ingredients

* 100g paneer
* 1 cup oats
* ½ cup mushrooms, chopped
* 1 cup spinach
* 1 onion, chopped
* 3–4 garlic cloves, chopped
* ½ tbsp ghee
* 1½ tbsp chili flakes
* 1 tbsp soy sauce
* ½ tbsp salt
* Water as needed

Directions

1. Heat ½ tbsp ghee in a pan. Add mushrooms, garlic, and chili flakes. Sauté for about 2 minutes.
2. Add the chopped onion and spinach. Sauté for 3–4 minutes until the onion softens and starts to caramelize.
3. Add soy sauce, salt, and water. Bring to a boil.
4. Add 100g paneer and 1 cup oats.
5. Keep stirring and cook until the oats are soft and the mixture reaches your desired consistency.
6. Divide into 2 servings and enjoy!

## 29. Halim seeds are rich in iron, but preparation matters.
**@leemamahajan** · 2026-08-07 · video · ❤ 26193 · https://www.instagram.com/p/Dbuz6hhpZJC/

Halim seeds are rich in iron, but preparation matters.

Soaking helps reduce antinutrients like phytates and oxalates, which can bind minerals and reduce their availability.

Research comparing processing methods found that boiling gave the highest ionizable iron, meaning more of the existing iron was in a form potentially available for absorption.

How to take it:

• Soak 1 tsp Halim seeds overnight.
• Discard the soaking water and rinse.
• Add 1 glass fresh water and lightly boil until soft.
• Consume the seeds with the cooking liquid.
• Once slightly cool, add lemon. Vitamin C improves non-heme iron absorption.
• Add ½ tsp ghee or another fat source to support absorption of fat-soluble compounds like vitamin E and carotenoids.
• Keep tea and coffee at least 1 hour away.

✅ Roasting is also useful, but boiling performed better for estimated iron availability in the comparative study.

✅ Another easy option is overnight-soaked Halim with a vitamin-C source + fat source.

👉🏻Save this method right now

## 40. 🌿 Thai Style Basil Tofu Fried Rice 🍚✨
**@pallilabandi** · 2026-07-23 · video · ❤ 1349 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DbHgtusufLF/

🌿 Thai Style Basil Tofu Fried Rice 🍚✨

Ingredients:

* 200 g firm tofu (cubed)
* 2 cups cooked rice (preferably day-old)
* 1 small onion (chopped)
* 4–5 garlic cloves (finely chopped)
* 2 green chillies (finely chopped)
* 1–1½ cups vegetables of your choice (carrot, bell pepper, beans, corn, broccoli, etc.)
* 1 bunch fresh basil leaves
* 1 tbsp soy sauce
* ½ tsp black pepper
* ½–1 tsp red chilli powder (optional)
* Salt to taste
* 2 tbsp rice flour or corn starch
* 1½–2 tbsp oil

👩‍🍳 Method:

1. Mix tofu with pepper, salt, and rice flour (or corn starch). Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 15 minutes or dry roast in a pan until golden.
2. Heat oil in a pan. Sauté garlic, green chillies, and onion until fragrant.
3. Add your favorite vegetables and stir-fry on high flame.
4. Add the crispy tofu and plenty of fresh basil leaves. Toss for a minute.
5. Add cooked rice, soy sauce, chilli powder (optional), and salt.
6. Toss everything on high flame for 2–3 minutes until well combined.

✨ Hot, comforting, protein-packed, and bursting with fresh basil flavor!

## 46. Zero-Oil Rice Paper Namkeen 🌶️✨

Zero-Oil Rice Paper Namkeen 🌶️✨

✅Save this easy recipe

Ingredients:

* Rice paper
* Salt
* Red chilli powder
* Chaat masala

Recipe:

1. Soak a rice paper sheet in normal water for 4–5 seconds.
2. Place it on a tray and sprinkle salt and red chilli powder evenly.
3. Cover it with another soaked rice paper sheet.
4. Cut it into any shape you like.
5. Carefully place the pieces in the air fryer basket and air fry at 160°C for 8–10 minutes, or until crisp.
6. Sprinkle chaat masala while it’s still warm and enjoy!

Tip: Store the namkeen in an airtight container to keep it crispy.

Fermented foods can physically bind toxins in your gut and carry them out. 

Most “fermented” food on shelves is pasteurized (heat-killed and useless)

The lactic acid bacteria that actually do the work:

Kimchi
- A kimchi strain (L. mesenteroides) held onto 57% of nanoplastics even in simulated gut conditions
- More than doubled plastic excretion in mice

Sauerkraut
- Lactobacillus strains removed up to 80% of lead and 75% of cadmium in lab tests

Miso
- Same class of bacteria bound up to 95% of arsenic from water within 4 hours

Kefir + yogurt
- Regular eaters had measurably lower phthalate metabolites in a study of ~8,000 people
- Phthalates are endocrine disruptors linked to lower testosterone and fertility

Look for “raw” or “live cultures” and check the refrigerated aisle. Pasteurized kraut, pickles, and miso do nothing

## 58. Protein Thepla 🔥
**@binalstastytales** · 2026-07-02 · video · ❤ 25083 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DaOsoM-AbMI/

Protein Thepla 🔥
15 Theplas. Approx 90g Protein. No Protein Powder.
Roll or No Roll (Press)

You took my protein roti to 550K asking for Part 2… so here it is. 💚

High-protein thepla made with real food — bajra, besan, @skotidakis_greek yogurt, Kirkland_signature organic firm tofu, sesame, spinach + methi.

No oil in the dough.
No protein powder.
Soft, freezer-friendly, and perfect for meal prep.

Batch: ∼90-92g protein | $4
Makes: 15 theplas
Each: ∼6g protein

Where’s the protein? No powder. Just food:
Bajra 26g + Besan 13g + Skotidakis 23g + Tofu 25g + Sesame 6g + Spinach 2g = 95g ✅

Recipe for 15 theplas:

Blend:
½ block firm tofu
1 cup full-fat greek yogurt 
Ginger-garlic-green chili paste
Haldi, red chili, dhaniya-jeera, salt

Mix with:
2 cups bajra flour or whole wheat flour
½ cup besan
3 cups chopped spinach + methi
¼ cup sesame seeds

Knead with blended paste.
No water. No oil in the dough.
Rest 10 min.

Roll thin or Press → Cook on hot tawa with just a touch of oil till it puffs.

Meal prep: Freezes 2 weeks. Reheat on tawa 30s.

Gujarati people: this is thepla.
Everyone else: call it methi paratha. 😄
Either way, it’s high-protein, filling, and made with simple ingredients.

## 64. Egg Semiya
**@kranthikitchen** · 2026-06-30 · video · ❤ 364011 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DaMb0rIqi6R/

Egg Semiya

2 eggs
1 cup semiya (vermicelli)
3 cups water
1 small carrot, finely chopped
6 beans, finely chopped
1 onion, sliced
Salt, to taste
1 tsp red chili powder
½ tsp black pepper powder
½ tsp garam masala
½ tsp turmeric powder
2 green chilies, slit
6–8 curry leaves
Fresh coriander, chopped (for garnish)
Method:
Dry roast or u can add little ghee to roast the semiya. Cook it in 3 cups of water until tender, then drain and set aside.
Heat a little oil in a pan. Add the eggs, salt, chili powder, and pepper powder. Scramble until cooked, then set aside.
In the same pan, heat a little more oil. Add the green chilies, curry leaves, and onions. Sauté until the onions turn translucent.
Add the turmeric powder and a little salt. Mix well, then add the carrots and beans. Sauté until the vegetables are cooked.
Add the cooked semiya and scrambled eggs. Sprinkle in the chili powder and garam masala, then toss everything together until well combined.
Garnish with fresh coriander and serve

## 76. High-Protein Veg Manchurian 😍
**@vaishali_living** · 2026-06-19 · video · ❤ 107204 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DZwc2G0BB0U/

High-Protein Veg Manchurian 😍
~36–39 g protein in the entire recipe 💪

👉 Manchurian Balls

🍀 Soak 60 g soy chunks in boiling water for 15 minutes. Drain, squeeze well, rinse 2–3 times, drain again, and finely chop or mince.

🍀 In a bowl, add finely chopped cabbage, carrot, and onion (about 500 g vegetables in total, with cabbage forming the major portion).

🍀 Add the chopped soy along with 1–2 tbsp coconut aminos, ½–1 tsp dark soy sauce, garlic, black pepper, red chilli sauce, and salt.

🍀 Add 2 tbsp rice flour + 2 tbsp potato starch/cornstarch and mix until the mixture binds together. If needed, squeeze out a little excess water from the vegetables (I didn’t, but definitely do if you’re planning to freeze)

🍀 Shape into balls and cook in a lightly greased appam pan on medium heat until golden and cooked through.

👉 Manchurian Sauce

🍀 In a pan, sauté 1 tbsp garlic, ½–1 tbsp ginger, chopped onion, and chopped capsicum.

🍀 Add coconut aminos, a little soy sauce, red chilli sauce, water, and a little potato starch slurry.

🍀 Cook until the sauce thickens slightly.

👉 Final Toss

🍀 Turn off the flame and add the prepared Manchurian balls.

🍀 Toss gently, garnish with spring onions, and serve hot.

## 94. Swap your guacamole for this iron-rich dip this summer: 
**@raquels.pantry** · 2026-05-31 · video · ❤ 125220 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DZA2JDxo_wu/

Swap your guacamole for this iron-rich dip this summer: 

Sikil Pak with Roasted Tomatoes, Charred Onion & Lime

Serves 6–8

Ingredients

* 1½ cups (200 g) pumpkin seeds
* 2 medium ripe tomatoes
* ½ small white onion
* 1 garlic clove*
* juice of 1 lime (originally orange juice) 
* 1/2 habanero, seeds removed (optional) 
* 3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
* ½ cup packed flat-leaf parsley (originally cilantro)
* ¾ tsp kosher salt
* 2–4 tbsp water, as needed

To Finish

* grated lime zest
* extra parsley leaves
* flaky salt

*For a lower-FODMAP version, replace the garlic clove with 1 tbsp garlic-infused olive oil.

Method

1. Toast the pumpkin seeds in a large dry skillet over medium heat until fragrant and lightly golden, about 4–5 minutes. Transfer to a bowl.
2. In the same skillet, char the tomatoes, onion, and garlic until softened and blistered in spots, about 8–10 minutes.
3. Add the toasted pumpkin seeds, tomatoes, onion, garlic, lime juice, olive oil, parsley, and salt to a blender.
4. Blend until smooth and creamy. Add 2–4 tablespoons of water as needed until the dip becomes silky but still holds its shape.
5. Taste and adjust with additional lime juice or salt if needed.
6. Spoon onto a serving plate and use the back of a spoon to create swoops and swirls.
7. Finish with a drizzle of olive oil, plenty of lime zest, extra parsley, and a pinch of flaky salt.

Enjoy <3

**@raquels.pantry** · 2026-05-18 · video · ❤ 13556 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DYfPzZ1IOkH/

In honor of Digestive Health Month, @seed and I saved one last drink recipe for the end. A drink I already made last summer and kept coming back to because it’s just that good. With a few small potential prebiotic perks and an updated recipe. 🌞

Cucumber, lime, raw honey, apple cider vinegar and sparkling water somehow turned into the drink everyone is going to make all summer. And we’re calling it now.

#SeedPartner #AD

Recipe:

* ½ cup homemade cucumber juice
* 1 tbsp fresh lime juice
* 1 tsp raw apple cider vinegar
* 1 tsp raw honey
* cucumber slices, lime slices & mint
* sparkling water + ice

For the cucumber juice: roughly chop a cucumber (you can peel it if you want a milder taste, but you don’t have to), blend until smooth and strain through a nut milk bag or very fine sieve.

Dissolve the honey in a splash of warm (not hot) water first, so it distributes evenly through the drink.

Then mix everything together, top with sparkling water and enjoy ice cold.

Little note: too much apple cider vinegar too often can be harsh on your teeth because of the acidity, so it’s best enjoyed through a straw.

Enjoy!

## 107. Soya & Chana Protein Balls 🌶️🧀
**@wifeofpotato** · 2026-05-18 · video · ❤ 18576 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DYex4oLzh6Z/

Soya & Chana Protein Balls 🌶️🧀

Ingredients

For the cheesy balls

* 50 grams crushed soya beans
* 50 grams boiled & mashed chana
* 1 boiled potato, mashed
* 1 small onion, finely chopped
* 3 tsp chopped spring onions
* Chopped green chillies
* Black pepper
* Oregano
* Chilli flakes
* Mozzarella cheese cubes (for filling)

For coating

* Finely chopped purple cabbage (squeeze out excess water)

Corn flour slurry

* 2–3 tbsp corn flour
* Water as needed
* Salt
* Black pepper
* Oregano
* Chilli flakes

Chipotle sauce

* 6–7 soaked dry red chillies
* 50 grams cashews
* 1 tsp curd
* 1/2 tsp sugar
* 3–4 garlic cloves
* 1/2 tsp oregano

⸻

Recipe

1. In a bowl, mix crushed soya beans, mashed chana, mashed potato, onions, spring onions, green chillies, black pepper, oregano, and chilli flakes.
2. Take a small portion of the mixture, place a mozzarella cube in the center, and shape into balls.
3. Prepare the slurry by mixing corn flour, water, salt, black pepper, oregano, and chilli flakes into a smooth batter.
4. Dip each ball into the slurry, then coat with finely chopped purple cabbage. Press gently so the coating sticks properly.
5. Air fry or shallow fry until golden and crispy from outside.
6. For the chipotle sauce, blend soaked red chillies, cashews, curd, sugar, garlic, and oregano until smooth and creamy.
7. Serve the crispy cheesy balls hot with the chipotle sauce.

Forget chia pudding, have this iron-rich aleev-subja pudding instead 

Women (unless pregnant) need 18 mg of iron daily, and just a spoonful of Aleev/ halim seeds- that have 100 mg of iron per 100 gms can help meet the daily requirement. 

I’ve paired it with cooling subja seeds since aleev is known to be heating, and also add some cardamom powder while cooking it.

Here’s the recipe, try it 

Combine 
2 tsp Aleev seeds
1 tsp subja 
Soak these in 1/2 a cup of water for 2 hours 

Once they are soaked and plump up, cook them in 
1/2 cup coconut milk + 2 Tbsp of water- use thick coconut milk, else it will split once the khareek is added 

Add 1/3 cup khareek, chopped into small pieces 

You need to cook this till it reaches a pudding my consistency- about 10 mins. Cook on low heat, while constantly stirring, else the milk can split after adding Khareek. 

Add some cardamom powder and turn off the flame. 
I recently added some saffron strands, and loved the flavour- you can try that too. 

You can have this also warm, but I personally like to cool it down, pair with some pomegranate (the Vitamin C helps with iron absorption) and some pumpkin seeds for texture.
You can drizzle some honey if you want it more sweet. 

A new favorite that both tastes and does good- try it!

## 133. Creamy Mushroom Open Toast 🍄🧀
**@chinmay.studio** · 2026-03-24 · video · ❤ 4708 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DWRCMq9jKpz/

Creamy Mushroom Open Toast 🍄🧀

Ingredients:

• 1 tbsp Butter
• 5-7 Garlic cloves (chopped)
• 1-2 Green chilies
• 1 Onion chopped
• 100 g Mushrooms
• 1 tbsp Wheat flour
• 1/2 cup Milk
• Oregano
• Chili flakes
• Salt
• Chilli oil
• Coriander

Method:
	1.	Toast the bread on both sides until crisp.
	2.	In butter, sauté garlic, green chilies & onion for 6–7 mins till caramelized.
	3.	Add mushrooms and cook till slightly crispy.
	4.	Add wheat flour, sauté for 1–2 mins.
	5.	Pour in milk (not too cold), mix well.
	6.	Add oregano, chili flakes & salt. Cook till creamy. Add chilli oil.
	7.	Add cheese & coriander, mix well.
	8.	Spread on toast & enjoy 🔥

Period pain laddoo 

📝 Haleem (Garden Cress) Laddoo – Notes Format

Ingredients:
	•	2 cups Haleem seeds (garden cress seeds)
	•	1 cup desiccated coconut
	•	2 cups jaggery powder
	•	2 tbsp ghee

Method:
	•	Soak Haleem seeds in water for 1 hour.
	•	Heat ghee in a pan.
	•	Add soaked seeds and roast for a few minutes.
	•	Add jaggery powder and desiccated coconut.

	•	Shape into small laddoos.
	•	Store in an airtight container (preferably refrigerated).

## 150. Recipe -
**@fit.khurana** · 2026-01-30 · video · ❤ 45275 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DUH_YkzDNla/

Recipe -

📝 Ingredients - 

• Black sesame seeds – ¾ cup
• Pumpkin seeds – ½ cup
• Walnuts – 10–12
• Dry coconut – 3–4 tbsp
• Makhana – 1 cup
• Ghee – ½ tbsp
• Anjeer – 8–10 medium (adjust to taste)
• Kishmish – 2 tbsp (optional)
• White sesame seeds – 2–3 tbsp, roasted (optional crunch)

👩‍🍳 Method - 

1️⃣ Dry roast the black sesame, pumpkin seeds, walnuts and dry coconut on low flame till aromatic and lightly golden. Let them cool completely.

2️⃣ In a blender, grind this roasted mix with ½ tbsp ghee till it turns into a smooth nut-seed butter.

3️⃣ Add the anjeer to the blender and grind again until you get a thick, glossy, sweet paste — no extra fat needed.

4️⃣ Separately dry roast the makhana till crisp, then grind into a powder.

5️⃣ Transfer the nut-anjeer paste to a bowl and mix in the makhana flour.

6️⃣ Add kishmish and roasted white sesame seeds if using. Mix well.

7️⃣ Portion into ~20 equal balls so each laddoo comes to roughly 90 calories.

8️⃣ Store in an airtight box.

## 171. Recipe ⬇️
**@fit.khurana** · 2025-12-29 · video · ❤ 112016 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DS2ESuHDACk/

Recipe ⬇️
Ingredients - 

Apologies, I missed the cals of one component while adding the ingredients, the total cals come to 422.

(25g Protein, 11g fiber, 422 cals)

✅For the filling - 
Boiled rajma – 100g
Tofu - 70-80g
Red chilli powder – ½ tsp
Black pepper – ¼ tsp
Jeera powder – ½ tsp
Salt to taste
Schezwan chutney – 1 tsp

Whole wheat tortilla or chapati – 1
Oil – 1 tsp (for cooking)

For the yogurt sauce - 
Greek yogurt – 2–3 tbsp
Chilli sauce – 1 tbsp

For the salsa - 
Tomato – 2-3 tbsp finely chopped
Fresh coriander – a handful
Lemon juice – 1 tbsp
Ketchup – ½ tbsp (optional)
Salt to taste

How to Prep ⬇️
🌸Mash the boiled rajma and tofu together with chilli powder, pepper, jeera powder, salt, and schezwan chutney until well combined.
🌸Slightly cook the tortilla on one side. Flip, spread the rajma–tofu mixture evenly on the cooked side, drizzle a little oil, and cook until golden and slightly crispy on both sides. 
🌸Mix Greek yogurt and chilli sauce to make a quick creamy sauce.
🌸In another bowl, mix tomato, coriander, lemon juice, ketchup, and salt to make the salsa. 
🌸Layer the sauce and salsa over the tortilla, fold into half, cut, and serve hot🔥

## 178. Palak Paneer✨ Cheese 🧀 Balls in Appam Pan🍁 | Crispy Bites🍃
**@sweet_n_sour08** · 2025-12-16 · video · ❤ 4735 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DSUvDX_E5mR/

Palak Paneer✨ Cheese 🧀 Balls in Appam Pan🍁 | Crispy Bites🍃
—
Ingredients:
250 g Blanched & finely chopped palak 
150 g Grated / crumbled paneer 
1/2 tsp Cumin powder
1/2 tsp Garam masala
1/2 tsp Salt - to taste
1 Green chilli, finely chopped
1 tsp Ginger-garlic paste
2 tbsp Cornflour 
2-3 tbsp Bread crumbs
1/4 cup mozzarella cheese small chunks 
Oil - for greasing & frying 
—
Method (Appam Pan):
1. In a bowl, mix palak, paneer, spices, chilli, ginger-garlic paste, salt, cornflour, and bread crumbs. Mix well and shape into a firm dough.
2. Make small lemon-sized balls. Stuff a small cheese cube inside each for a cheesy center. Seal well and roll into smooth balls.
3. Heat the appam pan on a medium flame and grease each cavity with a few drops of oil.
4. Place one ball in each cavity and cook for 1–2 minutes.
5. Gently rotate and turn the balls using a skewer or spoon, cooking until evenly golden and crisp on all sides (about 5–6 minutes total).
6. Remove once crisp on the outside and soft inside. Serve hot and enjoy! 😋
-

Hormones Balancing Kitchidi

Fiber is very important for hormonal health because it helps keep your hormones balanced naturally. It supports good digestion, which helps the body remove extra hormones like estrogen instead of reabsorbing them. Fiber also helps control blood sugar levels, which keeps insulin steady and prevents hormone ups and downs. A healthy gut fed by fiber improves how hormones work in the body and reduces inflammation that can disturb hormonal balance. It also helps you feel full, manage weight, and lower stress hormones. Eating enough fiber from fruits, vegetables, whole grains, seeds, and beans helps your hormones work more smoothly and keeps your body healthier overall.

## 183. Thecha Tomato Pakodas 🍅
**@kirtibhoutika** · 2025-12-11 · video · ❤ 16232 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DSIJ_sZk5pg/

Thecha Tomato Pakodas 🍅
Crispy outside, juicy inside — these stuffed tomato pakodas are my winter obsession!

Ingredients
For the Thecha:
	•	¼ cup peanuts
	•	4–5 garlic cloves
	•	2–3 green chillies
	•	1 tsp jeera
	•	A handful of fresh coriander (dhania)
	•	Salt to taste
	•	1–2 tsp oil

For the Pakodas:
	•	3–4 medium tomatoes, cut into thick slices
	•	½ cup besan
	•	2 tbsp rice flour
	•	½ tsp red chilli powder
	•	½ tsp ajwain
	•	Salt to taste
	•	Water as needed
	•	Oil for frying

Method
	1.	Make the Thecha: Heat oil in a pan and sauté peanuts, garlic, jeera, and green chillies until fragrant. Add chopped coriander and salt. Pulse everything into a coarse paste — don’t make it smooth.
	2.	Prep the Tomatoes: Cut tomatoes into thick slices and place a small spoon of the thecha in the centre of each slice.
	3.	Make the Batter: Mix besan, rice flour, red chilli powder, ajwain, and salt. Add water gradually to make a medium-thick batter.
	4.	Fry: Dip each thecha-filled tomato slice into the batter and deep fry on medium heat until golden, crisp, and sizzling.
	5.	Serve hot — the combo of crunchy coating + spicy thecha + soft tomato is unreal.

## 189. Green Macaroni (No Maida, No Cheese)

Green Macaroni (No Maida, No Cheese)

Day 4 of my 7-day series to help kids eat green vegetables! 🌿💚

Today I made Macaroni without maida and without cheese — a healthy twist to a kid’s favourite! Creamy, tasty and super light… even picky eaters will love this version.

Recipe⤵️
Boil water and add ¼ cup almonds with a little sugar. Turn off the flame and add chopped palak. Once it cools down, remove the skin of the almonds and blend everything together with paneer and garlic to make a smooth green sauce.

Now boil your macaroni and sauté your favourite veggies in olive oil.

Now, heat a pan and add a little Amul garlic butter. Pour in the green sauce, then mix in the boiled macaroni and sautéed veggies and salt. Garnish with oregano and chilli flakes, and it’s ready — creamy, healthy and delicious! 💚🍝✨

## 194. Delicious Corn Snack Recipe - Grandma’s Special ❤️ (Ammadi Recipe)
**@hemanth_varma51** · 2025-11-30 · video · ❤ 3658 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DRrWobGCPP2/

Delicious Corn Snack Recipe - Grandma’s Special ❤️ (Ammadi Recipe)

Traditional Andhra style corn snack recipe is simple, unique, and unbelievably delicious. 💯

FULL RECIPE: 👈
STEP 1 — Ingredients Prep
• Get fresh tender corn cobs (not sweet corn, normal corn).
• Cut them into small pieces as shown 
• Wash thoroughly and keep aside.

STEP 2 — Masala Ingredients 😊
• Curry leaves
• Onion paste
• Good thick curd
• Rice flour

STEP 3 — Masala Fry ❤️
1.	Turn on the stove, keep it on high flame, and take a cooker.
2.	Add a little oil.
3.	Once hot, add curry leaves, onion paste, salt, chilli powder, turmeric, and garam masala.
4.	Fry for a few seconds.
5.	Add the corn pieces you kept aside and toss until coated evenly.

STEP 4 — Curd Mixture 🧡
• Mix curd + rice flour + a little water until smooth.
• Add a little water to the corn in the cooker.
• Pour the curd mixture inside.

STEP 5 — Final Cook (Gravy Style Corn Snack) 🤫
• Do NOT close the cooker and don’t apply pressure.
• Keep on high flame and let it boil until texture starts forming.
• Switch to low flame and cook until it becomes slightly thick and gravy-like.

SERVE & ENJOY🫡
Serve hot in a bowl — the taste is unbelievable, spicy, creamy, and addictive! 🌽🔥
If you don’t eat it immediately… your mouth will crave it nonstop. Perfect evening snack, and  comfort food

## 197. For Day 18 of posting everyday until we reach 10K, let’s make this rich and creamy Lasooni Methi💚
**@urbanfoodfrenzy** · 2025-11-26 · video · ❤ 3890 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DRhQx2XjAc3/

For Day 18 of posting everyday until we reach 10K, let’s make this rich and creamy Lasooni Methi💚
Ingredients:
	•	1 bunch fresh methi, chopped
	•	10–12 garlic cloves (finely chopped)
	•	1 tbsp oil
	•	Salt to taste
	•	2 tbsp roasted peanuts
	•	1 tbsp roasted chana
	•	6–7 cashews
	•	1 tsp sesame seeds
	•	1 tbsp ghee or butter
	•	1 tsp jeera
	•	7-8 garlic , finely chopped
	•	1 onion, chopped
	•	1 tomato, chopped
	•	½ tsp turmeric
	•	1 tsp red chilli powder
	•	1 tsp coriander powder
	•	½ tsp garam masala

Method:
	1.	Chop your methi. Heat oil, add lots of garlic, then add the methi.
Season with salt, cook for 2–3 mins and keep aside.
	2.	Blend roasted peanuts, chana, cashews & sesame seeds into a smooth paste.
	3.	In a pan, heat ghee/butter, add jeera, garlic & onions and sauté.
	4.	Add tomatoes and cook them down.
	5.	Add haldi, red chilli, coriander powder & salt, then mix in the nutty paste.
	6.	Add garam masala, add the cooked methi back in and give everything a good mix.
	7.	Serve hot with phulkas — perfect for winter nights 🤍✨

## 206. Making sun-dried tomatoes at home is honestly a game-changer 🍅✨
**@lifewithshilpa** · 2025-11-16 · video · ❤ 15462 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DRHtuJTETAR/

Making sun-dried tomatoes at home is honestly a game-changer 🍅✨
So flavourful, so easy, and SO much better than store-bought!

Once you make a batch, you’ll keep finding new ways to use them:
• Toss into pastas or salads
• Blend into dips + spreads
• Add to sandwiches, wraps, pizzas
• Mix into homemade butter or olive oil
• Or just snack on them straight from the jar 😌

Sun, salt, patience… and you get pure MAGIC in a jar ☀️🍅
Try it once and you’ll never go back!

How to Make Them?👇🏻
-Wash the tomatoes and cut them into slices as shown in the video.
-Keep them in direct sunlight.
-Sprinkle salt on them generously and let them dry in the sun for 4 to 5 days or as required. There should be no moisture left in them. (You put the tomatoes in the sun during the daytime and at night, bring them inside your house.)
-Once the tomatoes have completely dried, rinse them under cold water to remove the excess salt in them.
-Spread the washed dried tomatoes on a kitchen towel. Pat them dry and let air-dry completely.
-Once dried, add them to a jar. Add any fresh herbs like rosemary, thyme or basil to enhance its flavour, I have used rosemary.
-Fill the jar with good quality olive oil. Make sure the tomatoes are submerged in olive oil. Add a pinch of salt. And then close the jar tightly with the lid. 
-Keep them aside for 15 days before using.

## 210. No Maida, No butter or oil - Sweet potato chocolate brownie ✨
**@auraartofhealthyliving** · 2025-11-14 · video · ❤ 282671 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DRCRRpjEtOi/

No Maida, No butter or oil - Sweet potato chocolate brownie ✨

Super fudgy, chocolatey and hits the right spot. I gave it to some of my family members and they couldnt guess it had sweet potatoes. 

Recipe:

Sweet Potato Chocolate Brownie (No maida, no oil, no butter)

Ingredients
	•	1 cup roasted sweet potato
	•	2 tablespoons jaggery or maple syrup
	•	2 tablespoons peanut butter
	•	1/4th cup cacao powder
	•	1 tablespoon chopped walnuts
	•	20–30 grams chopped dark chocolate chunks

Method
	1.	Chop the washed sweet potato and roast it in the air fryer at 180°C for 15–20 minutes.
If using an oven: roast at 200°C for 25–30 minutes.
	2.	Peel the roasted sweet potato and blend it with jaggery/maple syrup, peanut butter, cacao powder, walnuts, and chocolate chunks into a smooth paste.
	3.	Spread the batter in a baking tray lined with parchment paper.
	4.	Add extra chocolate chunks and walnuts on top.
	5.	Air fry at 175°C for 20–25 minutes.
If using an oven: bake at 180°C for 20–25 minutes.
	6.	Let it cool fully before slicing. Enjoy.

## 214. ✨ Coriander Lahsuni Roast ✨
**@ohmyvegggies** · 2025-11-12 · video · ❤ 15013 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DQ83NytjKA0/

✨ Coriander Lahsuni Roast ✨
Once in a blue moon my husband enters the kitchen… and this time he surprised me with this flavour-packed Coriander Lahsuni Roast! 🧄💚
Trust me, this one’s too good to skip — easy, comforting and pairs perfectly with paratha or lachcha onion!

👇 Here’s how to make it:

Ingredients for the marinade
	•	4 green chillies
	•	10–12 cashews
	•	7–8 garlic cloves
	•	1½ inch ginger
	•	7–8 curry leaves
	•	1 tbsp thick curd
	•	⅓ cup fresh cream
	•	½ bunch spinach (blanch in hot water for a few seconds, squeeze out excess water — don’t let the colour change)
	•	½ cup coriander leaves

Grind all of the above into a smooth paste.

For the soya:
	•	Soak 1 cup soya chunks in hot water for 10–15 mins till they swell up
	•	Squeeze out excess water
	•	Add 1 tbsp salt, ½ tsp turmeric, the prepared marinade, and juice of 1 lemon
	•	Let it rest for 15–20 mins

For cooking:
	•	Heat 3 tbsp oil
	•	Add 1 inch cinnamon stick, 1 black cardamom, 4–5 cloves, 2–3 green cardamoms, 1 large onion & few curry leaves
	•	Sauté till onions turn golden brown
	•	Add marinated soya and cook uncovered on medium-high till oil separates (don’t overcook or the colour darkens)
	•	Finish with ½ tsp garam masala & a drizzle of chilli oil (I used Chiliki) 🌶️

Serve hot with paratha and lachcha onions 🫶

## 216. 🌿 Iron and vitamin C rich Moringa Soup 🌿😍
**@_indian_tastebuds_** · 2025-11-10 · video · ❤ 6522 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DQ4N0UXjPqt/

🌿 Iron and vitamin C rich Moringa Soup 🌿😍
🥣 Ingredients
	•	2–3 cups fresh moringa leaves (drumstick leaves)
	•	2 medium onions, roughly cubed
	•	1 medium green tomato (or red, if preferred)
	•	5–6 garlic cloves, peeled
	•	1-inch piece ginger, peeled
	•	½ tsp cumin seeds
	•	¼ tsp turmeric powder
	•	½ tsp salt (adjust to taste)
	•	½ tsp black pepper powder
	•	1 tsp lemon juice
	•	1 cup hot water
	•	Coriander leaves for garnish
Method:
	1.	In a pressure cooker, add moringa leaves, onions, tomato, garlic, ginger, cumin seeds, turmeric, salt, and 2–3 cups water.
	2.	Pressure cook for 5 whistles.
	3.	Once cooled, blend into a smooth puree.
	4.	Transfer to a pan, add 1 cup hot water, pepper, and lemon juice.
	5.	Mix well, adjust salt, and simmer for 2–3 minutes.
	6.	Serve hot, garnished with coriander leaves and enjoy ☺️🌿

## 221. Your regular chapati just got a protein twist!” 💪🌿
**@dietwith_sanjana** · 2025-11-08 · video · ❤ 8016 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DQzMLkJDHjr/

Your regular chapati just got a protein twist!” 💪🌿
Tried this green gram protein chapati today and trust me, once you try it — you can’t get over the taste!
It’s not just soft and flavorful but also packed with protein and fiber that keeps you full for long hours.
Perfect for your weight-loss journey and a clean, balanced meal 

Green gram protein chapathi 
Ingredients:
1 cup whole wheat flour
1 cup soaked green gram (soaked overnight)
¼ onion
¼ carrot
Small piece of ginger
Few coriander stems
½ tsp fennel seeds
  Ajwain
Chopped onions (for mixing)
Chopped coriander leaves
Salt as per taste

Method (in 5–6 lines):
1️⃣ In a blender, add soaked green gram, onion, carrot, ginger, coriander stems & fennel seeds — blend into a smooth paste without water.
2️⃣ Take 2 spoons of this paste in a bowl.
3️⃣ Add 1 cup wheat flour, chopped onions, coriander & salt.
4️⃣ Mix well and knead into a soft dough.
5️⃣ Roll into small balls, flatten, and make chapatis.
6️⃣ Roast on a hot tawa till golden brown.

Kalasida Avalakki (Karnataka-style Poha Mix)

Kalasida Avalakki, the kind of snack that feels like home💛 something I’ve grown up eating almost every week and still crave on easy evenings!✨

📝Ingredients:
	•	2 cups thin poha
	•	½ cup onion, chopped
	•	¾ cup tomato, chopped
	•	½ cup capsicum, chopped
	•	¼–½ cup grated coconut
	•	1 tsp chilli powder
	•	1 tbsp chutney pudi
	•	Salt to taste
	•	1 tsp lemon juice
	•	A handful of coriander leaves, chopped

Tadka: 
	•	1–2 tbsp oil
	•	1-2 tbsp peanuts
	•	1 tsp mustard seeds
	•	1 tsp jeera
 •  1 tsp turmeric powder 
	•	A pinch of hing

Method:
	1.	In a bowl, add poha, chopped veggies, grated coconut, chilli powder, salt, chutney pudi, lemon juice, and coriander.
	2.	Heat oil and add mustard seeds, jeera, hing, and peanuts. Once roasted, pour this tadka over the poha mix, toss well, and serve fresh with some green chillies on the side if you like.

## 230. Homemade Ragi Choco Wafer Rolls
**@kidzapzoe** · 2025-10-31 · video · ❤ 1731 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DQdxVHCDByw/

Homemade Ragi Choco Wafer Rolls

My daughter’s a big fan of wafer rolls — so I finally made a homemade version & it’s a total win — tastes like store-bought wafer rolls but made with simple, healthier ingredients

Ragi adds iron, calcium & fibre, rice flour gives that crunch, and jaggery brings the sweetness alongwith cocoa powder for that rich chocolatey taste. 

You have a crispy, chocolaty snack that feels like a treat but sneaks in goodness too! 

Method: 
- In a bowl, mix ¼ cup ragi, ¼ cup rice flour, 1/2 cup jaggery, 4 tbsp cocoa powder, a pinch of salt, ½ tsp baking powder, ¼ tsp vanilla extract, 2 tbsp oil, and ½ cup warm milk.
 - Whisk everything together till you get a smooth, lump-free batter 
- Spread a thin layer of the batter on a waffle cone maker and cook till it turns slightly brown and crisp on the surface (You can use a nonstick tawa too)
 - Take it out while it’s still warm and roll it up quickly before it cools.
 - Once all the rolls are ready, dip them in melted dark chocolate or peanut butter and let them set.

## 234. Feeling bloated, gassy, or heavy after meals?  You’re not alone — bloating is super common and usually happens when dige
**@jonnas_kitchen** · 2025-10-29 · video · ❤ 888 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DQa76DqkWB4/

Feeling bloated, gassy, or heavy after meals?  You’re not alone — bloating is super common and usually happens when digestion slows down, causing food to ferment in the gut and trap gas. It can be triggered by eating too fast, stress, processed food, or an imbalance in gut bacteria. But the good news is, nature has your back! ✨

A simple kitchen remedy can bring quick relief — boil ½ tsp ajwain (carom seeds), ½ tsp zeera (cumin seeds), ½ tsp fennel seeds, and a pinch of dry ginger powder in 2 cups of water for 10 minutes, strain, and sip warm after meals. 💧

This ancient Ayurvedic blend works like magic for digestion. Ajwain boosts digestive enzymes and helps release trapped gas, cumin supports bile flow and reduces acidity, fennel relaxes the gut and prevents cramping, and dry ginger strengthens your digestive fire while calming inflammation. Together, they ease bloating, reduce heaviness, and keep your tummy light and comfortable. 🌸

Try sipping this herbal water daily after lunch or dinner for a few days — it’s a gentle, natural way to support your gut and feel more energized. 💚

## 247. Guilt free white sauce pasta ❤️
**@snap_snax** · 2025-10-14 · video · ❤ 22620 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DPyjvuIkgGi/

Guilt free white sauce pasta ❤️

🌿 Guilt-Free White Sauce Pasta

Ingredients:
	•	1 cup boiled cauliflower
	•	6–7 cashews
	•	100g paneer
	•	1 tsp butter
	•	1 tsp chilli oil
	•	3–4 garlic cloves, chopped
	•	1 cup chopped mushrooms
	•	1 cup chopped spinach
	•	Salt and pepper to taste
	•	½ tsp oregano
	•	½ tsp chilli flakes
	•	Boiled macaroni (as needed)
	•	Pasta water (to adjust consistency)

Method:
	1.	Prepare the Sauce Base:
Boil cauliflower and cashews till soft.
Blend them with paneer and a little water into a smooth, creamy paste.
	2.	Sauté the Veggies:
In a pan, heat butter, chopped garlic and chilli oil, then toss in mushrooms and spinach.
Cover and cook for 5 minutes till soft.
	3.	Make the Sauce:
Add the blended white sauce to the pan.
Pour in some pasta water to reach your desired consistency.
Season with salt, pepper, oregano, and chilli flakes.
	4.	Combine:
Add boiled macaroni and toss well to coat.
Let it cook for another 5 minutes till everything blends together.
	5.	Serve Hot:
Creamy, flavourful, and 100% guilt-free — your healthy white sauce pasta is ready! 🍝✨

## 254. Super crispy okra fries in the airfryer!!!!!! What a treat 
**@seemagetsbaked** · 2025-10-12 · video · ❤ 111329 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DPtbYEyiCDj/

Super crispy okra fries in the airfryer!!!!!! What a treat 

Okra fries

Ingredients
	•	250 g okra
	•	4 green chilies
	•	5–6 garlic cloves
	•	5 cm piece of ginger
	•	¼ tsp turmeric
	•	1 tsp ground coriander
	•	1 tsp ground cumin
	•	½ tsp chili powder
	•	1 tsp fine sea salt
	•	1 tsp garam masala
	•	2 tbsp gram flour (chickpea flour)
	•	2 tbsp self-raising flour
Method
- Blitz the ginger, garlic, and green chilies together, or crush them using a pestle and mortar.
- Combine the mixture with the dried spices, salt, gram flour, and self-raising flour.
- Slit the okra lengthwise into quarters to create thin strips. Toss the okra with the flour mixture and leave to rest for 30 minutes.
- Air-fry in batches on high for 12–15 minutes, or until crisp.
- Serve immediately

## 259. Homemade Dinner Scenes | Ep 49
**@niralichoksi_** · 2025-10-07 · video · ❤ 25963 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DPgkT4xiVI9/

Homemade Dinner Scenes | Ep 49

🌶️ Street Style Hakka Noodles (Indo-Chinese)
Serves: 2 🍽️ | Prep: 10 mins ⏱️ | Cook: 10–12 mins 🔥

🧄 Ingredients:
🍜 150–200g Hakka noodles (boiled)
🫒 2 tbsp oil (sesame/high-heat)
🧄 1 tbsp garlic, chopped
🥢 1 tsp ginger, chopped (optional)
🌶️ 1 green chili, slit/chopped
🧅 1 onion, thinly sliced
🫑 ½ capsicum, julienned
🥕 1 carrot, julienned
🥬 ½ cup cabbage, shredded
🧅 2 spring onions (white & green separated)

Sauces:
🧂 1 tbsp soy sauce (dark)
🍾 1 tsp vinegar
🌶️ 1 tbsp red chili sauce/ketchup
🖤 ½ tsp black pepper
🧂 Salt to taste

🔥 Method:
1️⃣ Boil noodles: Cook al dente, rinse with cold water, toss with a few drops of oil.
2️⃣ Heat wok: Oil on high flame until smoking. Add garlic, ginger & chili, sauté 15–20 sec.
3️⃣ Veggies: Toss onions & white spring onions 1–2 mins. Add carrot, capsicum & cabbage 2–3 mins (crisp).
4️⃣ Add sauces: Soy sauce, chili sauce, vinegar, pepper & salt. Mix well.
5️⃣ Combine noodles: Toss noodles 2–3 mins on high flame, carefully.
6️⃣ Serve: Garnish with green spring onions 🌿.

This High Protein Tofu Popcorn is the perfect guilt-free snack to munch on while keeping your macros in check. Serve it hot with a tangy-spicy yogurt dip and you won’t miss fried popcorn chicken again! 🍿
🥢 Recipe – High Protein Tofu Popcorn

Ingredients:
	•	200 g tofu (cut into bite-sized cubes)
	•	2 tbsp corn flour or oats flour
	•	1 tsp red chilli powder
	•	1 tbsp peri-peri powder
	•	Salt, to taste
	•	Brown bread crumbs, as needed
	•	Water, as needed

For the Sauce:
	•	60 g Greek yogurt
	•	1 tsp chilli oil
	•	1 tsp mustard sauce
	•	1 tsp honey
	•	Salt, to taste
	•	Juice of ½ lemon

Method:
	1.	Make slurry – In a bowl, mix corn/oats flour, chilli powder, peri-peri powder, salt, and some water into a smooth slurry.
	2.	Prepare dip – In another bowl, mix Greek yogurt, chilli oil, mustard sauce, honey, salt, and lemon juice until smooth. Keep aside.
	3.	Coat tofu – Dip tofu cubes into the slurry, then coat with brown bread crumbs.
	4.	Airfry – Preheat air fryer at 180°C for 5 minutes. Place tofu popcorns in the basket and air fry at 200°C for 12 minutes until golden and crisp.
	5.	Serve – Enjoy hot with the prepared yogurt dip.

Nutritional value (approx): 398 cal/per sandwich

Recipe (makes 1 sandwich) 

Prepare the spread →
 🌸 In a blender, add 50g low-fat paneer and 60g Greek yogurt (Epigamia/Skyr) and blend into a thick paste.

 🌸 Mix in finely chopped garlic, freshly ground pepper (adjust to your heat tolerance), chopped coriander leaves, lemon juice (missed in the video 🤦), salt, and a pinch of sugar to balance the flavours.

Prepare the filling →
 🌸 In a pan, heat ½ tsp oil, sauté minced garlic, then add 80g mushrooms with a pinch of salt (make sure they’re washed and cleaned properly).

 🌸 Cook until the water evaporates, then add 1 tsp soy sauce and cook on medium flame for another 2–3 minutes or until the mushrooms are soft and properly cooked.

 🌸 Add 30g baby spinach (if using regular spinach, blanch first), and cook for another minute.

Assembling →
 🌸 Layer the prepared paneer-yogurt spread on both slices of bread (about 50g sourdough for two slices).

 🌸 Add the sautéed mushrooms, 10g mozzarella, and some chili flakes.

 🌸 Heat ½ tsp butter in a pan and toast the sandwich on both sides until golden and crusty.

## 283. Because chocolates don’t always have to mean sugar and cocoa 🍫💛
**@growingupwithannika** · 2025-08-20 · video · ❤ 10386 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DNk8qAiyVHZ/

Because chocolates don’t always have to mean sugar and cocoa 🍫💛
Here’s a toddler-friendly version that looks like a treat but is packed with all the goodness of nuts, seeds, and fruits—a great way to add healthy fats, protein, and natural sweetness to your little one’s diet.

✨ Nut & Seed Chocolates (8M+) ✨

You’ll need:
	•	½ cup makhana
	•	½ cup mixed nuts (almonds, walnuts, cashews)
	•	¼ cup mixed seeds (pumpkin, sunflower, flax)
	•	7–8 dates
	•	2–3 figs

Method:
	1.	Roast makhana, nuts, and seeds until crunchy and aromatic.
	2.	Blend together with dates and figs until it forms a sticky mix.
	3.	Press into chocolate moulds or roll into small balls.
	4.	Refrigerate 15–20 mins, then de-mould.

That’s it—nutritious, cocoa-free chocolates ready in minutes!
A wholesome snack for babies 8 months and above… and honestly, adults love them too 🤭✨

## 287. Instant Sambar in Minutes! 🥘✨ Make once, enjoy anytime. No time? No problem! ⏱️ This Sambar Premix = comfort food made 
**@anusharjunn** · 2025-08-18 · video · ❤ 11259 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DNe8dhjyeVk/

Instant Sambar in Minutes! 🥘✨ Make once, enjoy anytime. No time? No problem! ⏱️ This Sambar Premix = comfort food made easy 🤩
.
Instant Sambar Premix

Ingredients:
•	Toor dal – 1 cup
•	Chana dal – ¼ cup
•	Moong dal – 1 tbsp
•	Urad dal – 1 tbsp
•	Fenugreek seeds – ½ tbsp
•	Rice – 1 tbsp
•	Coriander seeds – 1 tbsp
•	Black pepper – ½ tbsp
•	Mustard seeds – 1 tbsp
•	Cumin seeds (Jeera) – 1 tbsp
•	Dry red chillies – 1 cup
•	Curry leaves – 1 cup
•	Tamarind – ½ cup
•	Turmeric powder – 1 tsp
•	Salt – 2 tbsp

Method:
1.	In a kadai, dry roast the toor dal, chana dal, moong dal, urad dal, fenugreek seeds, and rice on low flame until they turn crisp. Transfer to a plate and allow to cool.
2.	In the same kadai, dry roast coriander seeds, black pepper, mustard seeds, and cumin seeds on low flame. Set aside to cool.
3.	Next, roast the dry red chillies, curry leaves, and tamarind in the same kadai until crisp. Let them cool completely.
4.	First, grind the roasted red chillies, curry leaves, and tamarind into a fine powder.
5.	Add the roasted dal–spice mixture to the same jar, along with turmeric powder and salt. Grind everything together into a fine powder.
6.	Store in an airtight container. Your Instant Sambar Premix is ready to use.

Note: In the video, the red chillies appear darker as they were slightly over-roasted. While making, roast them only until they turn crisp — avoid over-roasti …

Packed with fiber, plant protein, and micronutrients

Keeps you full on a weight loss diet

Easy to prepare as a quick go-to dinner recipe

Great for kids as an after-school snack to prevent constipation

**@__ritikaajain** · 2025-07-22 · video · ❤ 3 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DMbM-Yxtp7S/

Share it with someone who needs this easy super diet friendly stuffed mushrooms. They are the perfect bite-sized delight—creamy, cheesy, and packed with flavor! 🍄✨ Made with fresh spinach, crumbled feta, and a hint of garlic. For the protein you can add paneer too. 
Who’s craving a bite? 
deets⬇️
8 mushrooms 
1 cup spinach (chopped)
½ cup feta cheese (crumbled)
1 small onion (finely chopped)
2 cloves garlic (minced)
1 tsp butter
½ tsp black pepper
½ tsp chili flakes (optional)
1 tsp oregano 
Salt to taste
Instructions:
• Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
• Prepare mushrooms – Remove the stems carefully, chop them finely, and set aside.
• Sauté filling – Heat olive oil in a pan, add onions, garlic, and chopped mushroom stems. Cook for 2-3 minutes. 
• Add spinach and cook until wilted. • Add spices and herbs. Turn off the heat. Once cooled down, mix in feta cheese.
• Stuff the mushrooms – Spoon the spinach-feta mixture into the mushroom caps.
• Bake – Place on a baking tray and bake for 12-15 minutes or until mushrooms are tender.
• Serve warm and enjoy!

## 320. Shorn fatty acidts (SCFAs), primarily acetate, propionate, and butyrate, are important metabolites produced by gut bacte
**@jonnas_kitchen** · 2025-07-10 · video · ❤ 7797 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DL7g4jRvACR/

Shorn fatty acidts (SCFAs), primarily acetate, propionate, and butyrate, are important metabolites produced by gut bacteria through the fermentation of dietary fibers and resistant starches in the colon. These molecules play a vital role in maintaining gut health, as butyrate serves as the primary energy source for colon cells and helps maintain the integrity of the intestinal lining, reducing the risk of gut inflammation and "leaky gut" syndrome. SCFAs also have powerful anti-inflammatory properties and are known to regulate immune function by influencing the activity of immune cells and suppressing harmful inflammatory responses. Beyond the gut, SCFAs contribute to metabolic health by regulating blood sugar and lipid metabolism, supporting cholesterol balance, and stimulating the release of hormones that control appetite, such as GLP-1 and PYY. Additionally, SCFAs are involved in the gut-brain axis, potentially affecting mood and brain function through signaling pathways and neurotransmitter modulation. Their presence in the body has been associated with a reduced risk of various chronic diseases, including obesity, type 2 diabetes, colorectal cancer, and inflammatory bowel diseases. A diet rich in dietary fiber, resistant starches, and prebiotics helps support the production of SCFAs, thereby promoting overall health and well-being.

Instructions (detailed recipe breakdown on my Substack💛):
- Rinse rice with cold water until mostly clear. Drain.
- Add sprouted lentils + soaked beans to rice. Gently mix. 
- Add 2 cups water. Let it sit for 5 mins.
- Cook in rice cooker on white rice setting OR on stovetop (bring to boil → cover → low simmer for 16-18 min → let rest at least 10 min)
- Before serving, give it a gentle mix. Enjoy!

## 327. Today I’m sharing a delicious Dhaba-style Kasuri Methi Curry a famous dhaba dish in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh!
**@nikhitha_vangaru** · 2025-07-04 · video · ❤ 13997 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DLqyng5g5p6/

Today I’m sharing a delicious Dhaba-style Kasuri Methi Curry a famous dhaba dish in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh!

Start by heating 4 tbsp oil in a pan. Add 1 tbsp jeera and saunf, then 3–4 green chilies and 1 finely chopped onion. Sauté until golden brown. Add a pinch of turmeric and 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, let it fry well.

Next, add 1 finely chopped tomato. Cook until it softens and oil separates. Then, add 1½ tbsp Kasuri Methi and finely chopped fresh methi leaves. Let all the moisture evaporate.

Now add cashew paste (made from ½ cup cashews soaked in hot water and ground to a smooth paste). Pour in a little water for consistency and let it cook well.

Add salt, red chilli powder, garam masala, and jeera powder. Mix and cook thoroughly.

Finally, add paneer cubes and some grated paneer. Simmer on low flame for 10 minutes.

That’s it — rich, creamy, flavorful Kasuri Methi paneer curry, Dhaba-style! 🤤

## 339. Ep 25 of Weight Loss Recipes
**@soulfulswaad** · 2025-06-19 · video · ❤ 8850 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DLFL1mLTzCW/

Ep 25 of Weight Loss Recipes

Healthy Veggie Fried Rice

Main Ingredients
	•	Cooked cold rice
	•	Oil
	•	Garlic
	•	Green chili (optional)
	•	Onion
	•	Red capsicum
	•	Yellow capsicum
	•	Green capsicum
	•	Mushroom
	•	Baby corn
	•	Broccoli
	•	Beans
	•	Carrot
	•	Paneer

Spices & Seasonings
	•	Salt
	•	Black pepper
	•	Oregano
	•	Red chili flakes (optional)
	•	Kashmiri chili powder (used instead of chili flakes)
	•	Garam masala
	•	Cumin powder

Sauce Mix
	•	Soy sauce
	•	Vinegar
	•	Red chili sauce

⸻

Steps
	1.	Heat oil in a wok or pan.
	2.	Add garlic and green chili. Sauté until aromatic. (Skip the green chili if using chili flakes.)
	3.	Add onion and cook until slightly soft.
	4.	Add all vegetables except paneer — capsicums, mushroom, baby corn, broccoli, beans, and carrot.
	5.	Sauté on high heat for a few minutes. Don’t overcook.
	6.	Add salt, pepper, oregano, red chili flakes or Kashmiri chili powder, garam masala, and cumin powder. Adjust to taste.
	7.	Add paneer and sauté lightly.
	8.	Pour in the sauce mix (soy sauce, vinegar, red chili sauce). Mix well.
	9.	Add cold rice and combine gently.
	10.	Sauté for a few more minutes, adjust seasoning if needed — and it’s ready to serve.

## 340. Marshmallows from Marshmallow Root 🌿
**@saraganeshpandy** · 2025-06-18 · video · ❤ 1007791 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DLCfJ0bSTDm/

Marshmallows from Marshmallow Root 🌿

After three earlier attempts, I finally mastered it on my fourth try—and it was worth every bit of the learning! 🤗

  Soak  1 tablespoon of marshmallow root in  1 cup of water and let it infuse overnight. This will be your base.

  Use half a cup of the strained marshmallow water and mix it with 3 tablespoons of gelatin ( or 1 tablespoon of agar agar) Let it bloom and sit.

  In a separate pot, combine the remaining half cup of marshmallow water with 1 cup of sweetener and a pinch of salt . Stir well until dissolved and bring it to a boil. Heat the mixture until it reaches the **soft ball stage** (around 240–245°F / 115–118°C**), which should take  8 to 9 minutes.

  Begin whipping the bloomed gelatin mixture, then gradually pour the hot syrup into it from the side as you continue whipping. Whip until it’s fluffy and holds shape.

  Dust a parchment-lined tray with arrowroot or starch powder, pour in the whipped mixture, and smooth it out. Let it sit at room temperature for at least 6 hours. Do not refrigerate.

These taste incredible when toasted over a flame and enjoyed immediately.

Note : If you wanna try this and don’t have marshmallow roots ,just replace them with plain water ….It will be just sweet version without any marshmallow benefits :) But it will be worth trying 🤗

These little bites are loaded with:
🌱 Biotin for hair & nails
💪 Iron & protein from seeds
🥥 Healthy fats for energy
🍬 Sweetened only with dates

Instructions:-

1. Soften Dates
In a pan, add ghee and the dates. Cook on low for few minutes until soft. Mash into a paste or blend it smooth once slightly cool.

2. Dry Roast Seeds & Nuts
In another pan, dry roast all seeds and nuts (pumpkin, sunflower, chia, flax, sesame, hemp, coconut, walnuts, almonds) on low heat for 3–5 minutes until aromatic.

3. Grind to Powder
Cool the roasted mix and grind it into a coarse powder.

4. Mix & Bind
Add the powder to the date paste and mix well. If the mixture is too dry, warm it slightly to soften.

5. Shape into Balls
Roll into small ladoos using your palms. You can coat them in coconut or crushed seeds if desired.

6. Store in an airtight container for up to 10 days at room temp or refrigerate for longer shelf life.

📝 Ingredients (for ~500g batch)

🌿For Air-Frying:
	•	Soya chunks – 130g
	•	Moong dal – 100g
	•	Salt – ½ tsp (each)
	•	Red chilli powder – ½ tsp (each)
	•	Chaat masala – ½ tsp (each)
	•	Oil (optional) – ½ tsp (each)

🌿For the Mix:
	•	Roasted chana – 50g
	•	Jowar puffs – 80g
	•	Ragi puffs – 60g
	•	Cold-pressed oil – 2 tsp
	•	Garlic paste – 1 tsp
	•	Curry leaves – 2 sprigs
	•	Dry red chilli – 1
	•	Hing – a pinch
	•	Salt – to taste
	•	Black salt – ½ tsp
	•	Chaat masala – 1 tsp
	•	Amchoor – ½ tsp

—

🔥 Air-Fryer Prep:

Soya Chunks:
	1.	Soak in hot water (15–20 mins), rinse, squeeze, and air dry.
	2.	Toss with salt, red chilli powder, chaat masala.
	3.	Air-fry at 180°C (356°F) for 10–12 mins, shaking halfway, till golden.

Moong Dal:
	1.	Soak 4–5 hours or overnight → strain → air dry 20–30 mins.
	2.	Toss with spices.
	3.	Air-fry at 180°C (356°F) for 10–15 mins, shaking every 5 mins.

—

## 352. you don't wanna miss this pahadi chaunsa dal⬇️
**@__ritikaajain** · 2025-05-29 · video · ❤ 3 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DKNZ4NGtqxM/

you don't wanna miss this pahadi chaunsa dal⬇️
• 1/2 cup whole or split black urad 
• 3 garlic cloves 
• 1inch ginger
• 1 green chili
• 1 tsp cumin seeds
• 1 tsp coriander seeds 
• 6-7 peppercorns 
• 2 tbsp fresh coriander 
• mustard oil
• 1/2 tsp mustard seeds
• hing
• 1/2 tbsp aata
• 1/2 tsp turmeric powder 
• salt
• 1 tsp coriander powder 
method :
~ Dry wipe dal with kitchen towel then roast in a kadhai for upto 4-5 mins. Then grind coarsely.
~ To make the paste - In mortar and pestle, pound garlic, ginger, green chilli, cumin seeds, coriander seeds, fresh coriander and, black peppercorns. 
~ For the dal, heat mustard oil, add mustard seeds, red kashmiri mirch, prepared paste and hing. Cook nicely. 
~ Add ground dal, aata and mix. Further add water, turmeric, salt, coriander powder. Mix. 
~ Cover and let it simmer until the dal gets cooked completely. You might need to add more water as it thickend up later. 
~ serve with rice and ghee🫶👌

**@shivesh17** · 2025-05-17 · video · ❤ 352226 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DJnw6T1vwLb/

Ready to make the easiest suji bread at home? It’s so much better and softer than store bought one and I’m sure you’ll love making this eggless, no maida, no oven bread! 

Ingredients 
🍞1+1/2 cup suji
🍞1 tsp instant yeast 
🍞1 tbsp castor sugar
🍞1/4 tsp salt
🍞3 tbsp milk 
🍞1/2 cup water 
🍞2 tbsp oil 
🍞3 tbsp mixed seeds, to top

Method 
1. In a blender jar add 1+1/2 cup suji and finely grind it.
2. Add suji, yeast, sugar  and salt in a bowl and give it a good whisk.
3. Now add in water, milk, oil and mix using a wooden spoon to form a batter.
4. Let the batter rest for 10 minutes.This will ensure that semolina has absorbed all the water.
5. After 10 minutes,transfer the dough onto a greased surface and knead it for around 15 minutes.
6. To check if the dough is ready to proof, take small piece of dough  and gently stretch it between your fingers . If the dough can be stretched thin enough and light passes through it , it means the dough is ready and it has passed the windowpane test.
7. Once the dough is formed,transfer it in a large bowl greased with oil. Cover the bowl with a cloth and let it proof for 1 hour in a dark warm place  or until doubled in volume.
8. Knock down the dough after the first proofing.
9. Roll out the dough into a rough  rectangle of 1/2 inch thickness.Then starting from one shorter end , roll in the dough for form a log. Make sure to pinch and lo …

Healthier version of samosa

✅Recipe details: 
To make the dough,mix 1 cup wheat flour,1/4th cup rava,1/2 tsp ajwain,1 tbsp sesame seeds,salt as per taste,mix it well and add 2 tbsp ghee or oil
Mix the ghee with flour nicely and make a semi soft dough by adding normal water

To make the filling,take a silbatte and grind 1tsp cumin seeds,1 tsp coriander seeds,1 tsp saunf,in the same silbatta,grind some ginger and green chilies 
Now in a Kadhai add 1 tbsp ghee,add the ground powder and sauté ,now add ginger green chilli paste and cook 
Now add 3 boiled potatoes,some aamchur powder,Garam masala and Kasuri methi 
Add some boiled green peas and salt as per taste 
Mash everything together and cook for 1 minute,after that let this cool for sometime 
Divide the dough in same equal parts,I’ve made 12 exact portions of this dough 
Stuff the aloo filling and cube of paneer in it and seal it nicely 
Cook these balls in a paniyaram/appe pan on low flame till they becomes golden in colour and khasta 
It took me 10 minutes to cook them perfectly 
Serve them hot with some tamarind chutney and enjoy!!!

Who knew makhana could get this chatpata? 

This pani puri-style makhana is my latest snack hack for kids. Makhana is naturally rich in calcium, iron, and antioxidants, making it one of the best snacks to support growing bones and boost immunity 

This one is perfect for tiffins, movie nights, or anytime snack cravings :) 

Recipe: 
- In an air fryer, dry 1 bowl curry leaves, 1 bunch mint leaves & 1 bowl coriander individually at 180*c for 10-15mins
- They should become nice and crisp
- Now grind them all together with black salt, 4-5 peppercorns, chaat Masala, pani puri masala and some mishri (rock sugar) 
- Dry roast 2 bowls of makhana
 Then heat 2 tbsp ghee, add 2 tbsp of the masala and finally the makhana. Mix well till the masala coats the makhana and it’s ready.

✨ No Sugar No jaggery No Cream Chocolate Ice Cream – Guilt-Free 🍫❄️

Craving ice cream but skipping sugar, jaggery, or cream? Here’s your fix! Would you try this wholesome chocolate delight made with makhana and dates? 🤎

🥄 A naturally sweet, protein-packed frozen treat using clean pantry ingredients—creamy, rich & perfect for summer cravings!

🌿 Ingredients:
✔ ¼ cup makhana
✔ 2 tbsp oats
✔ Handful of mixed nuts
✔ 4–5 seedless dates
✔ 1 glass warm milk (to soak)
✔ 1 tbsp cocoa powder
✔ ½ tsp coffee powder (optional)

🥄 How to Make:
1️⃣ Soak makhana, oats, nuts, and dates in warm milk for 10–15 mins.
2️⃣ Transfer to a mixie jar, add cocoa & coffee powder.
3️⃣ Blend until smooth & creamy.
4️⃣ Transfer to a container, sprinkle choco chips (optional).
5️⃣ Cover with cling film, touching the surface.
6️⃣ Freeze overnight or for 10–12 hours.
7️⃣ Scoop & enjoy your no-guilt chocolate ice cream!

## 402. If you’ve ever wondered why sea salt is used in kimchi instead of iodized salt…here’s why:
**@thesimplelivingproject** · 2025-04-18 · video · ❤ 60974 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DIlssZIzl8D/

If you’ve ever wondered why sea salt is used in kimchi instead of iodized salt…here’s why:
Iodine can interfere with fermentation. Sea salt helps draw out moisture from the cabbage without disrupting the natural process. That’s step one, and it sets the tone for the entire batch.

Here’s the recipe I followed for this small batch:

⸻

Ingredients

Salting:
	•	1 medium napa cabbage (about a kg)
	•	1/4 cup sea salt

Base:
	•	1/2 cup water
	•	1 tsp rice flour (or all-purpose flour)
	•	1 tsp sugar (you can skip sugar and blend in a piece of apple or pear for natural sweetness)

Seasoning Paste:
	•	2 tbsp gochugaru (I used 3 for extra heat)
	•	1 tbsp minced garlic
	•	1 tsp minced ginger
	•	1 tbsp fish sauce (or soy sauce for vegetarian version)
	•	1/4 cup julienned radish (optional)
	•	1/4 cup green onion, chopped
	•	1/4 small carrot, julienned (optional)

⸻

Steps:
	1.	Salt the cabbage and let it wilt for 1–2 hours. Wash thoroughly and squeeze out excess water.
	2.	Cook the rice flour paste, let it cool.
	3.	Mix it with the seasoning ingredients.
	4.	Combine with the cabbage and pack into a sterilized jar.
	5.	Leave at room temp for 24 hours to ferment, then refrigerate.

You’ll know fermentation has kicked in when you catch that slightly sour, garlicky funk. That’s the good stuff.

Every batch is a bit of a flavor experiment and that’s what makes it fun. Save this if you’re ready  …

## 405. When you’re in the mood for something a little more filling and familiar, this Veg Shami Kebab Pav hits the spot.
**@borosilandyou** · 2025-04-16 · video · ❤ 3542 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DIfvVYhSsOK/

When you’re in the mood for something a little more filling and familiar, this Veg Shami Kebab Pav hits the spot.

Soya chunks add the perfect texture, while everyday masalas do their quiet magic. Toasted pav, a bit of green chutney, and lunch suddenly feels a lot more special.

Ingredients:
For the Kebab:
● 1 cup soya chunks
● 1 small onion, finely chopped
● 2 tbsp coriander leaves, chopped
● 1 green chili, finely chopped
● Salt to taste
● 1⁄2 tsp turmeric
● 1 tsp red chili powder
● 1 tsp garam masala
● 2 tbsp besan (gram flour)

For Serving:
● Pav (soft bread rolls)
● Crispy potato salli (thin fried potato sticks)
● Lemon wedges
● Sliced onions
● Shikanji (Indian spiced lemonade)

Instructions:
1. Prepare the Soya Chunks:
○ Soak the soya chunks in hot water for 10 minutes.
○ Squeeze out excess water and blend into a coarse paste.
2. Make the Kebab Mixture:
○ In a bowl, mix the soya paste, chopped onions, coriander, green chili, salt,
turmeric, red chili powder, garam masala, and besan.
○ Combine well to form a dough-like mixture.
3. Make the Chutney:
○ In a blender, add coriander, green chilies, ginger, garlic, salt, and lemon juice.
○ Blend until smooth.
4. Shape and Fry:
○ Divide the mixture into small patties.
○ Heat oil in a pan and shallow-fry the kebabs until golden brown and crisp on
both sides.
5. Assemble the Pav:
○ Apply chutney, onion slices, mayo, and a kebab insi …

## 407. My 17th Weight Loss Recipe 👇. Calories around 350
**@vencutcook** · 2025-04-10 · video · ❤ 1426 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DIQ7q6_Jx7G/

My 17th Weight Loss Recipe 👇. Calories around 350

Protein 25g

1. Low fat and high protein paneer 100g
2. Mushrooms 100g
3. 1/2 Capsicum cubes
4. 1/2 carrot circle 
5. 10ml coconut oil
6. 1/2 onion sliced
7. 2 tsp garlic chopped
8. 1 tsp ginger chopped
9. 2 green chilli chopped
10. Hand full of coriander leaf 
11. Big 1/2 lemon
12. 1 tsp light soya sauce
13. 1 tsp pepper powder
14. 1/2 tsp sugar
15. 1 tbsp corn flour
16. 500ml water
17. Salt

Preparation of this recipe

1. Take a pan
2. Add oil, onion, garlic, ginger, green chilli, small amount of coriander leaves.
3. Sauté it all for 1 min in high flame.
4. Now add carrot, capsicum, mushrooms 
5. Mix it all in high flame for 2 mins
6. Now add water
7. Let it boil
8. Add soya sauce, pepper powder, salt.
9. Mix it for 1 min in high flame.
10. Now add corn flour slurry (take a cup add 1 tbsp corn flour add 4 tbsp water mix it and add into the sauce)
11. Mix in it high flame for 30 secs.
12. After sauce become thick, add paneer, bunch of coriander leaf, squeeze half lemon juice.
13. Mix it all for 2 mins in high flame.
14. Sauce will become more thick.
15. Now check the taste if you feel more tangy or spicy or sour, add the sugar.
16. It will even the taste.
17. Mix it for 30 secs.
18. Check the salt and switch off the flame.
19. Serve it with Rice
20. Don’t share it and enjoy it for yourself!!!

## 426. Grilled Rajma Quesadilla! 
**@nids.lid** · 2025-03-11 · video · ❤ 5456 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DHDqHS0y42-/

Grilled Rajma Quesadilla! 

📝Ingredients:
- 1 cup boiled rajma (red kidney beans) 
- ½ cup chopped onion 
- ½ cup chopped tomato 
- ½ cup chopped capsicum 
- ½ cup boiled corn 
- 1 tsp red chili flakes 
- 1 tsp oregano 
- Salt to taste 
- 1 tbsp hot sauce 
- Leftover chapati or roti 

Method:
1. In a bowl, mix boiled rajma, onion, tomato, capsicum, and corn. 
2. Add red chili flakes, oregano, salt, and hot sauce(or chipotle mayo). Mix well. 
3. Heat a grill pan and place a chapati on it. 
4. On one half of the chapati, sprinkle some cheese, top with the rajma mixture, and top again with more cheese. 
5. Fold the chapati in half and gently press. 
6. Grill on both sides until golden brown and crisp. 
7. Serve hot with your favorite dip and enjoy! 

Thanks to @bergnerindia for the Argent Samsara Grill Pan—its tri-ply build and non-stick coating make grilling effortless!✨

Recipe:

• In a pan (i used same pan), add lil more butter, grated garlic, wheat flour & fry until the raw smell of wheat flour goes away.

• Let it boil and come together. 
• You can add cheese at this point
• Add the pasta mixture to Sauce & mix well until Combined. 
• Serve Hot

## 439. My whole family & my hormones love this recipe 🤍✨🍕 - HIT SAVE AND TRY IT🤍🌸
**@fitnesswithkeisha** · 2025-03-01 · video · ❤ 1114 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DGpytauMJ4_/

My whole family & my hormones love this recipe 🤍✨🍕 - HIT SAVE AND TRY IT🤍🌸

✨ 1 large sweet potato (cut into thick rounds)
✨1 tbsp olive oil
✨½ tsp garlic powder, paprika
✨½ tsp dried oregano, pepper
✨Salt & pepper to taste
✨ ¼ cup tomato sauce (low-sugar) I use @mr_organic 
✨ ½ cup shredded cheese (mozzarella or dairy-free alternative)
✨ Toppings: Bell peppers, cherry tomatoes, spinach, mushrooms, olives, cooked chicken, etc.

Instructions:
1️⃣Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
2️⃣Prepare the bases: Toss the sweet potato rounds with olive oil, garlic powder, oregano, salt, and pepper.
3️⃣Bake: Arrange on a lined baking tray and bake for 15 minutes, flipping halfway.
4️⃣Assemble: Spread tomato sauce on each round, sprinkle cheese, decorate with your favourite toppings!
5️⃣Bake again: Pop them back in the oven for 5-7 minutes until the cheese melts.
6️⃣Enjoy! Serve with a side of hummus or Greek yoghurt dip.

## 441. Spicy Sizzling Cheesy Corn Dip😍🌽🧀🌶️
**@ohyumness** · 2025-02-28 · video · ❤ 38753 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DGmuvaaICWd/

Spicy Sizzling Cheesy Corn Dip😍🌽🧀🌶️

You know ever since I had tried the iconic cheese, chilli and corn mixture, I knew I loved it, in any form and variant and this Sizzling Cheesy Corn Dip is actually a showstopper.😋

Easy, cheesy and yumm - all that I ever need my food to be😂

How to?
🧈 2 tbsp butter
🥵 1 tbsp green chillies 
🫑 1/3 cup capsicum 
🌽 1 cup boiled sweet corn
- Start by melting butter in a pan and add chillies, capsicum and corn. Mix well.

🌾 1.5 tbsp wheat flour
🥛 2 cups milk (or as required)
🌶️ 1 tbsp chilli flakes
🌿 1 tsp oregano
🧂 salt as per taste
🧀 Cheese (mozzarella and processed both)
🥄 1 tsp sugar (optional & I did not add)
✨ Jalapeños (optional but adds a good flavour/ garnish)
- Mix in the flour and add milk in batches while continuously stirring it to avoid forming lumps.
- Once it starts bubbling, add herbs and seasoning along with cheese.
- Add more cheese on top while it’s hot and cover it for 10 minutes or until the cheese melts.
- Garnish with jalapeños/ finely chopped coriander.

Serve with chips, nachos, and toasted bread (best)🥐
Tip - Adjust the consistency before serving if required.

Share this with your friends and family. Save it for future reference.💌

## 443. Let's make Instant Millet dosa,this is gluten free recipe.A single millet dosa gives 87 calories and 4gm proteins.It is 
**@dietkundali24** · 2025-02-27 · video · ❤ 16709 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DGkP1fDI2ZI/

Let's make Instant Millet dosa,this is gluten free recipe.A single millet dosa gives 87 calories and 4gm proteins.It is loaded with veggies.

Jowar Instant dosa

Serving-9 dosa

Ingredients

1-Jowar atta-1 cup(130gm)

2-Paneer-100gm

3-Onion-40gm

4-Carrot-50gm

5-Green chili-as per taste

6-Coriander leaves-2tbsp

7-Till-2tsp

8-Jeera powder-1 tsp

9-Turmeric powder-1/4th tsp

10-Coriander powder-1tsp

11-Salt-as per taste

12-Oil-few drops to grease the tawa

Method

1-Wash and grate the carrot and paneer.

2-Chop Onion, chili, coriander leaves finely.

3-In a bowl add jowar atta(you can use any millet atta, or gehu atta), add 2 cups water and mix well.Make sure there is no lumps.

4-Now add all chopped vegetables and spices and salt, mix well.

5-Keep it aside for 10 mins.

6-Again add 2 cups water and mix well, batter consistency should be flowy.

7-Heat the non stick tawa, grease it with little oil.

8-Pour the better on tawa, cook it on slow to medium flame.

9-Serve hot with any chutney.

Soya rotis are made with well-balanced proportions of boiled soya chunks paste, besan and wheat flour for a protein-packed punch.

Soya Roti is rich in Folic Acid, Magnesium, Phosphorus, Vitamin B1, 2, Protein.

Tips for soya roti: 
1. Remember to leave the dough alone for 15 minutes so as to get the perfect, elastic consistency for easy rolling. 

2. Don’t cook soya chapati on the open flame for too long or else the they will burn and become hard.

You can pack soya roti with paneer curry, veggies, sprouts and other healthy combinations and make it a wholesome meal. 

Macronutrients (per Roti)
Calories: 110 kcal
Protein: 8g
Fats: 2g
Carbs: 15g
Fiber: 3g

Ingredients: (12 Roti)
Soya Chunks, 200g
Besan, 120g
Wheat flour, 120g
Water as needed.
Salt to taste

Instructions: 
1. Boil Soya chunks for 5 minutes. Drain and let cool.
2. Transfer into a blender, add salt and masala. Make a paste.
3. Knead a dough with Soya Paste, Besan, Atta. Cover and keep aside for 15 minutes. 
4. Make regular chapattis with this atta.

Protein Dosa

🥄 1 cup Chopped tender coconut (Use grated for babies under 1 year)

🌱 2 tsp Sabja seeds (soaked)

5️⃣ Unmold, enjoy & stay cool! 🌞❄️

## 459. SHARE ✅ 
**@goal_together_** · 2025-02-21 · video · ❤ 692 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DGVUEU0yYH7/

SHARE ✅ 
High Protein: Supports muscle repair, weight loss, and energy levels. 
Rich in Fiber: Aids digestion and gut health.
Low Glycemic Index: Helps regulate blood sugar, good for PCOS & diabetes.
Boosts Iron & Calcium: Supports bone and overall health.
Hormone Balancing: Ideal for women with thyroid issues or hormonal imbalances.

Ingredients:
	•	¼ cup Green Moong
	•	¼ cup Rajma (Kidney Beans)
	•	¼ cup Horse Gram
	•	¼ cup Black Chana
	•	¼ cup Soya Beans
	•	½ cup Idli Rice
	•	¼ cup Urad Dal
	•	½ tsp Fenugreek Seeds

Preparation Steps:
	1.	Soak:
	•	Wash all lentils, beans, rice, and fenugreek seeds.
	•	Soak them together in enough water for 8-10 hours or overnight.
	2.	Grind:
	•	Drain the soaked ingredients and grind them into a smooth batter using little water.
	•	The batter should be of medium consistency (not too thick or thin).
	•	Add salt as needed and let it ferment overnight (6-8 hours).
	3.	Cook:
	•	Heat a dosa tawa, lightly grease it with oil.
	•	Pour a ladle of batter and spread it in a circular motion to make a thin dosa.
	•	Cook on medium heat until golden brown. Flip and cook the other side if needed.
	4.	Serve:
	•	Serve hot with coconut chutney or sambar.

## 461. 🌿🥟Iron Rich Moringa Millet Kolukattai 🥟🌿
**@utiram.krithika** · 2025-02-20 · video · ❤ 5096 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DGR2iDTPGvn/

🌿🥟Iron Rich Moringa Millet Kolukattai 🥟🌿

A nutritious twist to traditional kolukattai with moringa flowers & millets—perfect for a wholesome snack! 💚✨

🌾 Ingredients:
🔸 Moringa flowers - 1.5 cups
🔸 Onion - 1 (chopped)
🔸 Carrot - 1 (chopped)
🔸 Beans - ½ cup (chopped)
🔸 Capsicum - ½ cup (chopped)
🔸 Cabbage - ¾ cup (chopped)
🔸 Corn - ½ cup
🔸 Salt & chili flakes - as needed
🔸 Grated coconut - 1 cup (optional, but enhances taste 🥥)
🔸 Pani varagu (Proso millet) - 1.5 cup (or any millet of choice)

🍽 Method:

1️⃣ Wash & soak millet for 2 hours, then grind into a thick batter.
2️⃣ In a pan, sauté onions, carrots, beans, capsicum, cabbage, corn, & moringa flowers until soft. 🌿🥕
3️⃣ Add salt, chili flakes & grated coconut. Mix well! 🌶️🥥
4️⃣ Combine the veggie mix with the millet batter & make small dumplings. 🏵️
5️⃣ Steam for 10-12 mins until firm & cooked through. 🍃✨

Enjoy this healthy, flavorful kolukattai as a perfect snack or breakfast option! 😍🌱

## 473. Homemade Tomato Ketchup (Not recommended for babies under 2 years)🍅✨
**@utiram.krithika** · 2025-02-12 · video · ❤ 34042 · https://www.instagram.com/p/DF9QyJxvbJu/

Homemade Tomato Ketchup (Not recommended for babies under 2 years)🍅✨

Make your own fresh and flavorful tomato ketchup at home with simple ingredients!

Ingredients:

🍅 Tomato – 500g
🧄 Garlic – 7 to 8 cloves
🌶️ Red Chilly – 1
🧂 Salt – as needed
🍯 Brown Sugar – 1 cup
🍋 Lemon Juice – 2 tsp

Method:
1️⃣ Chop & Cook: Roughly chop tomatoes and garlic. In a pan, add tomatoes, garlic, red chilly, and a pinch of salt. Cook on low flame until tomatoes turn soft and mushy.
2️⃣ Blend & Strain: Let it cool, then blend into a smooth puree. Strain to remove seeds and skin.
3️⃣ Cook Again: Pour the strained puree back into the pan, add brown sugar, and simmer until thick.
4️⃣ Final Touch: Add lemon juice and mix well. Let it cool completely.
5️⃣ Store & Enjoy: Transfer to a glass jar and refrigerate. Use it with your favorite snacks!

💡 Tip: For a thicker consistency, cook for a little longer on low flame.

Try this easy homemade ketchup and enjoy the fresh, preservative-free goodness! 🍅❤️

Use it occasionally and don’t offer it on a daily basis.
